authored_explainer.title: Cereal Production Is 1.5x Its 1972 Level
authored_explainer.hook: The 1970s food panic missed what global harvests did next.
says: Progression to secondary school rose from 77.8% in 1985 to 91.3% in 2017 — 1.2 times higher.
Cereal production climbed from 1083.7 million metric tons in 1972 to 1644.1 in 2024 — 1.5 times higher.
China has 5.2 million square kilometers of farmland; United States 4.2, Australia 3.6, Brazil 2.4, and Russia 2.2.
authored_explainer.closing: The famine everyone predicted never arrived because output kept rising.
authored_explainer.question: What changed food production most?

authored_explainer.title: Combustible Renewables And Waste Are 3.0x Higher Than In 1990
authored_explainer.hook: One energy source tripled since 1990, and it is not solar or wind.
says: Combustible renewables and waste rose from 10.2% of energy in 1990 to 30.1% in 2024 — 3.0 times higher.
Electricity access climbed from 73.2% in 1998 to 91.9% in 2024 — 1.3 times higher.
Waste methane emissions rose from 903.8 Mt CO2e in 1972 to 1,652 in 2024 — 1.8 times higher.
authored_explainer.closing: A third of the world's energy now comes from things once thrown away.
authored_explainer.question: Which number surprised you most?

authored_explainer.title: Population Growth Fell 54% Since 1972
authored_explainer.hook: Population growth was expected to accelerate forever. The data says it reversed.
says: Rural population fell from 63.1% in 1972 to 42.2% in 2025 — down to 67 percent of its former share.
The largest city's share barely moved: 18.2% of urban population in 1972 versus 16.2% in 2025.
Population growth fell from 2% annually in 1972 to 0.91% in 2025 — down to 46 percent.
authored_explainer.closing: The planet is still growing, but it has almost stopped accelerating.
authored_explainer.question: Which shift surprised you most?
